name: quantum-classifier-evaluation
title: Quantum Classifier Evaluation — GenotypeToPhenotypeProcess on Synthetic Multi-Omic Data
question: Can the GenotypeToPhenotypeProcess match or exceed classical ML baselines in predicting binary phenotypes from synthetic multi-omic data?
objective:
Train the GenotypeToPhenotypeProcess with M=4 modalities, F=6 features per
modality on synthetic data, and compare accuracy, AUC-ROC, F1, precision,
and recall against RF and LR baselines.
hypothesis: The quantum classifier will achieve competitive AUC-ROC (>= 0.80) on synthetic data with strong cross-modality interactions, benefiting from the CNOT entanglement chain.

study_card.goal: Evaluate the multi-qubit quantum classifier against classical baselines.
study_card.mechanism: Each omic modality maps to a dedicated qubit via Rot encoding. A CNOT chain entangles all qubits. Qubit 0's fidelity to the 'viable' state gives the classification score. Adam optimizer, MSE cost, 6 epochs.
study_card.why_before_next: This is the central evaluation for the investigation's primary research question.
study_card.expected_result: Quantum AUC-ROC within 0.05 of RF baseline; F1 >= 0.70.

description: This study runs the GenotypeToPhenotypeProcess on synthetic multi-omic data with 4 modalities, 6 features per modality, 60 training and 100 test samples, 0.15 noise. The circuit uses M qubits, Rot encoding, pre-entanglement rotations, a CNOT chain, post-entanglement rotations, and fidelity measurement on qubit 0. Training: 6 epochs, Adam (lr=0.4), batch size 16. The interactive Marimo notebook provides a walkthrough with live plots and classical ML benchmarks computed side-by-side.
expected_behavior: Quantum classifier AUC-ROC is within 0.05 of the Random Forest baseline AUC-ROC.
Quantum classifier F1 score exceeds 0.70 on held-out test data.
Training loss converges below 0.25 by the final epoch.
